messages:
Jordan H: hey everyone, just joined — trying to run my dev container (Colima on macOS Ventura) and can't reach internal registry git.packages.redwood.local while on corporate L2TP VPN (split-tunnel). host can curl the registry but container DNS returns NXDOMAIN.
Mira D: welcome! Colima spins a Linux VM; it usually inherits host DNS but split-tunnel VPNs can leave the VM without the internal nameserver. can you paste `scutil --dns` on mac and `/etc/resolv.conf` inside the container?
Jordan H: host scutil shows nameserver 10.12.0.5 for search domain redwood.internal. inside container `/etc/resolv.conf` shows `nameserver 1.1.1.1` and no search. ping by IP works if i `ssh -L 5000:10.12.4.20:5000 bastion.redwood.com` on host and curl localhost:5000 (host ok) but container->localhost:5000 times out.
Sam M: two problems: DNS and host->container networking. For DNS: start container with `--dns 10.12.0.5` or edit colima's dns config (`colima start --dns 10.12.0.5`). For networking: Colima uses a VM NAT; use `--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway` or publish the forwarded port to the VM network.
IT Ops: note: L2TP clients sometimes push `exclude 0.0.0.0/0` style split; confirm your VPN includes 10.12.0.0/16 in routes. if not, ask VPN team to push route or add to local routes: `sudo route -n add -net 10.12.0.0/16 192.168.1.1` (replace gateway).
Jordan H: tried `colima start --dns 10.12.0.5` and `docker run --rm --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway curlimages/curl curl http://host.docker.internal:5000` 50ms latency and returns 200! registry/pull works inside container now. thanks for the quick help :tada:
infra-bot: ticket INF-5022 created to add Colima+L2TP note to onboarding docs (assigned eng-infra).
Mira D: adding a short checklist to the new-hires doc: "If using Colima/Colima VM or Docker Desktop on mac and on split-tunnel VPN, add VPN DNS to Colima and use host-gateway for forwarded ports."
Jordan H: saved me hours, appreciate it :heart:
